rationale: Both series demonstrated excellent fidelity to the codebase. Series A has a more logical and beginner-friendly pedagogical flow, starting with the modern `from_provider` abstraction. However, Series B wins due to its superior coverage of advanced, production-oriented features. Its tutorials on `create_iterable`, `create_partial`, and the `BatchProcessor` provide developers with the knowledge to tackle complex, real-world problems at scale. The 'Practical Applications' tutorial in Series B is a significant differentiator, connecting library features to tangible, high-value use cases like RAG and large-scale data extraction. While its pedagogical structure could be improved (the 'Core Concepts' deep-dive is too early), its depth and comprehensiveness make it the more valuable technical resource overall.
